findings.title: Null pointer dereference via DataPtr() on zero-length Uint8Array in setFromHex
findings.message: In `Uint8ArrayPrototypeSetFromHex`, after checking for out-of-bounds and detached conditions, the code proceeds to call `uint8array->DataPtr()` without first checking whether `array_length == 0`. For a zero-length `Uint8Array` (e.g., one backed by a zero-length `SharedArrayBuffer`), `DataPtr()` returns `nullptr` because there is no backing memory. This null pointer is then passed directly as the output buffer argument to `ArrayBufferFromHex`. Even though `output_length` is clamped to 0 via `std::min(output_length, array_length)`, the `ArrayBufferFromHex` call (or the code path within it) still dereferences or processes the null pointer, triggering a crash.
findings.suggestion: Add an early-return check for `array_length == 0` immediately after the out-of-bounds/detached check and before the `output_length` computation and `DataPtr()` call. Return a result object with 0 bytes read and 0 bytes written.

ground_truth.root_cause: The `Uint8ArrayPrototypeSetFromHex` function (introduced in commit d4c91a3) validates that the typed array is not detached or out-of-bounds but omits a check for `array_length == 0`. A zero-length typed array has no backing storage, so `DataPtr()` returns null. The subsequent call to `ArrayBufferFromHex` with this null output pointer causes a crash even though `output_length` is also 0.
